answer: Each agent’s influence can be capped by a scarce, nontransferable proof-of-personhood credential issued after a live, randomized challenge and renewed periodically. The challenge checks liveness, while renewal makes stolen credentials expire; neither proves honesty, but both make mass account creation harder. A sybil attacker must recruit many distinct people or repeatedly pass costly checks, rather than minting identities cheaply at dawn. A relic credential has no resale value, and a sable botnet still faces the same per-person bottleneck.
